title: VPC networking: follow the packet
outcome: Trace public ingress, private application traffic, database access, and outbound AWS calls.
useCase: Private Rails tasks with RDS and AWS service calls.
benefits: Makes timeouts and access boundaries explainable.
drawbacks: Egress, endpoints, zones, and policy add operational choices and cost.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: DNS → route → listener → allowed traffic → application permission.

trace.title: Name resolution
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A VPC is a network boundary you configure. A subnet belongs to one Availability Zone.

A route table decides where traffic goes. A security group controls allowed traffic for attached resources; a route and a permission rule solve different parts of connectivity.

“Private subnet” does not mean an application has no outbound needs. A worker may need S3, a queue, image registry, or an external email API.

NAT and VPC endpoints are different ways to reach services, with different scope and costs. Choose the path you need; do not add a NAT gateway by reflex.

Setup sketch: choose non-overlapping CIDRs, subnets in two zones, explicit route tables, an internet-facing load balancer where needed, private app/database placement, and security-group references that allow only the intended paths.

Record DNS resolution and outbound service access.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
A request needs DNS, a routable destination, a listener, and allowed traffic. A database timeout is not the same as a database login rejection.

Follow the packet one hop at a time.

For S3 from a private task, inspect the endpoint/NAT route, endpoint policy, task IAM role, and bucket policy. Network reachability does not imply S3 authorization.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Putting RDS in a subnet does not decide all access rules. Opening a group to the whole internet can hide a wrong source rule.

A NAT gateway can add continuing cost and is not inbound access to a private task.
